neighbours.label: ' on' directly after 'up' (up on the roof, got up on stage)
fire: The boy scrambled up on the wall to watch the parade.
When the music started she hopped up on a chair and waved.
Two climbers were stranded up on the ridge overnight.
The goat had somehow got up on the roof of the shed.
A crowd gathered while he stood up on the stage alone.
Our tent was pitched high up on the hillside.
The kitten leapt up on the counter and knocked over a cup.
The flag was raised up on the tower at dawn.
quiet: The boy sat on the wall to watch the parade.
When the music started she stood on a chair and waved.
Two climbers were stranded near the ridge overnight.
The goat had somehow got onto the roof of the shed.
A crowd gathered while he stood alone on the stage.
Our tent was pitched high in the hills.
The kitten walked across the counter and knocked over a cup.
The flag was raised over the tower at dawn.

notes: Card: ' on' x26, all 'up on'; opposite pole is ' to' after 'up' ('up to date'). Probe: 'climbed up on the shelf' 0.44, 'jumped up on the table' 0.56; 'sat on the shelf' 0.002; 'up the ladder' 0.09.
